references.text: God says 'Do not be afraid' to Israel, his little flock, and promises to help them. Isaiah uses the same expression 'do not be afraid' (μὴ φοβοῦ) that Jesus uses in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32], directed toward God's chosen people as a small and vulnerable remnant.
The Lord says 'Do not be afraid' to Jacob/Israel and assures them of his care. The same comforting address from God to his people that Jesus gives to the disciples in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32].

In Daniel's vision, the kingdom and dominion are given to 'the saints of the Most High,' that is, God's people. This corresponds to the Father's decision to give the kingdom to the little flock in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32].
'The saints of the Most High' will receive the kingdom and possess it forever. The Father's gift of the kingdom to the disciples in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32] fulfills this promise to the holy ones.
The Lord gathers the lambs like a shepherd and carries them close to his heart. The image of God as shepherd for his little flock (ποίμνιον) echoes in Jesus' words in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32].

God promises to be himself the shepherd for his flock and to seek out the lost. The image of God as shepherd for his flock (ποίμνιον) is the background for Jesus' words about 'the little flock' in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32].

Jesus praises the Father because it has 'pleased' (εὐδοκία) him to reveal this to the childlike. The same thought of the Father's good pleasure (εὐδόκησεν) as in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32], where the Father gladly gives the kingdom to the small ones.
Jesus says, 'I give you the kingdom, just as my Father has given it to me.' This is a direct parallel to [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32] where the Father gives the kingdom to the disciples.

God has chosen the poor in this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom he promised those who love him. A parallel to [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32] where the small, seemingly insignificant flock receives the kingdom as a gift.

Jesus refers to his disciples as his sheep and assures them that no one can snatch them out of the Father's hand. The image of the disciples as a flock under the Father's protection parallels 'the little flock' in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32].

The prophet says, 'Do not be afraid, Zion,' and assures that the Lord is among his people like a mighty savior. The same encouragement not to fear that Jesus gives to the little flock in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32].
Peter urges the elders to shepherd God's flock (ποίμνιον). The same word for 'flock' is used as in [ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32], and the church is understood as God's sheepfold that needs care.
